findings.description: Anthropic continuation v1 stores only the most recent assistant_content, and every follow-up request is rebuilt as original prompt plus that latest assistant block plus the current result block. A three-tool-round control showed the fourth request retained only a3/a3 and dropped a1/a1 and a2/a2. Anthropic tests assert only one follow-up batch, while OpenAI has a strict three-round accumulated-transcript assertion.
findings.impact: The two dialects do not have symmetric multi-round context guarantees. A stateless Anthropic endpoint can lose earlier read/edit evidence and make a later verify/final decision from incomplete context.
findings.required_followup: Open a separately owned product-and-test ticket that freezes an Anthropic red test equivalent to TEST-059-C, preserves the complete ordered stateless transcript across rounds, and reruns dual-dialect adjacency before AUDIT-059-A is repeated.

findings.description: OpenAI v2 transcript validation enforces call-ID uniqueness, prior-call ordering and result-ID uniqueness, but never requires the set of result IDs to equal the unresolved call IDs. An in-memory negative control supplied two function calls and one result; compile_request accepted it and prepared transport input with calls=2/results=1.
findings.impact: The adapter does not independently fail closed on a dropped result, despite the native contract's one-call/one-result invariant and the handoff claim that every function output is present exactly once.
findings.required_followup: Open a separately owned Responses test/fix ticket that freezes missing, extra, duplicated and reordered multi-call result controls, requires exact unresolved-call/result set equality before transport, and retains the existing v1 fail-closed behavior.

findings.description: The manifest freezes fake-provider call IDs such as v2-b-command, and verify_scenario requires those literal IDs in Runtime safety evidence for both fake and authorized_live execution. Real provider call IDs are opaque and generated at response time, so a conformant authorized live run cannot satisfy the literal required_call_ids/denied_call_id checks.
findings.impact: The harness is correctly fail-closed and no live run occurred, but the handoff's authorized_live_supported claim is not operational: a future authorized smoke will fail verification even when Runtime correctly denies the actual provider call ID.
findings.required_followup: Open a separately owned human-smoke harness correction that derives semantic call roles from observed model-exchange events, binds denial and continuation checks to those exact observed provider call IDs, retains the no-intent-leak prompt, and keeps the fake fixture deterministic.
